nodes.name: Gradient–exponential relation on 2x2 matrix groups
nodes.statement: Let $\exp: \mathbb{C}^{2\times 2} \to \mathbf{GL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$ be the matrix exponential function \cite{absil2009optimization,baker2012matrix,Hall15:lie} sending $\matr{\Delta}$ to $\exp(\matr{\Delta})$. \\ (i) If $h:\SUNN{2}(\mathbb{C})\to\mathbb{R}$ is a differentiable function and $\matr{\Delta}\in\mathfrak{su}_2(\mathbb{C})= \Tang{\matr{I}_2}{\SUNN{2}(\mathbb{C})}$, we have that \begin{equation} \langle\matr{\Delta},\ProjGrad{h}{\matr{I}_2}\rangle_{\matr{I}_2} = \left.\left( \frac{d}{dt} h (\exp(t\matr{\Delta}) )\right)\right|_{t=0}. \end{equation} (ii) If $h:\mathbf{SUT}_2(\mathbb{C})\to\mathbb{R}$ is a differentiable function and $\matr{\Delta}\in\mathfrak{sut}_2(\mathbb{C})= \Tang{\matr{I}_2}{\mathbf{SUT}_2(\mathbb{C})}$, we have the relationship \cref{eq:gradient_exp_map-2}. \\ (iii) If $h:\mathbf{SLT}_2(\mathbb{C})\to\mathbb{R}$ is a differentiable function and $\matr{\Delta}\in\mathfrak{slt}_2(\mathbb{C})= \Tang{\matr{I}_2}{\mathbf{SLT}_2(\mathbb{C})}$, we have the relationship \cref{eq:gradient_exp_map-2}.\\ (iv) If $h:\mathbf{D}_2(\mathbb{C})\to\mathbb{R}$ is a differentiable function and $\matr{\Delta}\in\mathfrak{d}_2(\mathbb{C})= \Tang{\matr{I}_2}{\mathbf{D}_2(\mathbb{C})}$, we have the relationship \cref{eq:gradient_exp_map-2}.
nodes.label: lem:gra_rela_elem

nodes.name: Gradient–exponential relation at I_2
nodes.statement: \langle\matr{\Delta},\ProjGrad{h}{\matr{I}_2}\rangle_{\matr{I}_2} = \left.\left( \frac{d}{dt} h (\exp(t\matr{\Delta}) )\right)\right|_{t=0}.
nodes.label: eq:gradient_exp_map-2

nodes.name: Proof of the Riemannian gradients of the elementary functions
nodes.statement: Define a projection operator $\mathcal{P}_{i,j}: \mathbb{C}^{m\times m} \to\mathbb{C}^{2\times 2}$ extracting a submatrix of $\matr{X} \in \mathbb{C}^{m\times m}$ as in \cite[Eq. (3.7)]{ULC2019}, and $\mathcal{P}_{i,j}^{{\sf T}}: \mathbb{C}^{2\times 2} \to\mathbb{C}^{m\times m}$ the conjugate operator. For the elementary function $\hij{i}{j}{\matr{X}}$ defined in \cref{eq:elemn_func_h}, if $\matr{\Delta} \in \mathfrak{su}_2(\mathbb{C}) = \Tang{\matr{I}_2}{\SUNN{2}(\mathbb{C})}$, we have that \begin{align*} &\langle\matr{\Delta},\ProjGrad{\hij{i}{j}{\matr{X}}}{\matr{I}_2}\rangle_{\matr{I}_2} = \left.\left( \frac{d}{dt} \hij{i}{j}{\matr{X}} (\exp(t\matr{\Delta}) )\right)\right|_{t=0} \ \ (\text{by \Cref{lem:gra_rela_elem}(i)}) \\ &= \left.\left( \frac{d}{dt} g (\matr{X} \Gmat{i}{j}{\exp(t\matr{\Delta} )} )\right)\right|_{t=0} = \left.\left( \frac{d}{dt} g (\text{Exp}_{\matr{X}} (\matr{X}\mathcal{P}_{i,j}^{{\sf T}}(\matr{\Delta} )t )) \right)\right|_{t=0} \\ &= \langle\matr{X} \mathcal{P}_{i,j}^{{\sf T}}(\matr{\Delta}),\ProjGrad{g}{\matr{X}}\rangle_{\matr{X}} \ \ (\text{by equation}\ \cref{eq:gradient_exp_map})= \langle\matr{\Delta},\mathcal{P}_{i,j} (\matr{\Lambda})\rangle_{\matr{I}_2}, \end{align*} where $\text{Exp}_{\matr{X}}$ is the map defined in \cref{eq:Exp_x_sl}. Note that $\matr{\Delta} \in \mathfrak{su}_2(\mathbb{C})$ and $\ProjGrad{\hij{i}{j}{\matr{X}}}{\matr{I}_2} \in \mathfrak{su}_2(\mathbb{C})$. The result can be obtained by direct calculations. For other three elementary functions $h^{(U)}_{(i,j),\matr{X}}$, $h^{(L)}_{(i,j),\matr{X}}$ and $h^{(D)}_{(i,j),\matr{X}}$, similar as the above case, we can obtain the results by \Cref{lem:gra_rela_elem}(ii), \Cref{lem:gra_rela_elem}(iii) and \Cref{lem:gra_rela_elem}(iv), respectively. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Compute directional derivatives along exp(tΔ) via the gradient–exponential relation and identify the projected submatrix of Λ.

nodes.name: Two elementary complex inequalities
nodes.statement: (i) If $z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{C}$, then \begin{equation*} |z_1-z_2|^2 + |z_2|^2 \geq \frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}(|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2). \end{equation*} (ii) If $\{z_i\}_{1\leq i\leq m}\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ satisfy $\sum_{1\leq i\leq m}z_i=0$, then \begin{equation*} \sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m}|z_i-z_j|^2 = m\sum_{1\leq i\leq m}|z_i|^2. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lemma-ai-sum-0_c

nodes.name: Proof of well-definedness of Subalgorithms 1a and 1b
nodes.statement: (i) We first prove the existence of such an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_{k}$ in \autoref{alg:jacobi-LU-G_c}. By \Cref{lem:ProjGradSubmatrix_2}, \Cref{lemma-ai-sum-0_c} and $\matr{\Lambda}=\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\in\mathfrak{sl}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$, we have that \begin{align*} &\sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(\|\partial h^{(U)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2+\|\partial h^{(L)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2+\|\partial h^{(D)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\right) \\ &= \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{j_ki_k}|^2\right) + m\sum_{1\leq i_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_ki_k}|^2 \geq \|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2. \end{align*} Therefore, there exist an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k=h^{(U)}_k, h^{(L)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$ such that $\frac{3}{2}m(m-1)\|\partial h_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\geq\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2$. \\ (ii) We now prove the existence in \autoref{alg:jacobi-LQ-G_c}. Similar as above, we get that \begin{align*} &\sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(\|\partial h^{(Q)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2+\|\partial h^{(U)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2 + \|\partial h^{(D)}_k(\matr{I}_2) \|^2\right) \\ &= \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}^{*} - \Lambda_{j_ki_k}|^2+|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{i_ki_k} - \Lambda_{j_kj_k}|^2\right)\\ &\geq \frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{j_ki_k}|^2\right) + m\sum_{1\leq i_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_ki_k}|^2 \geq \frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2. \end{align*} Therefore, there exists an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k =h^{(Q)}_k, h^{(U)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$ such that $\frac{3}{3-\sqrt{5}}m(m-1)\|\partial h_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\geq\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2.$ The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the squared partial derivatives over all pairs and elementary functions to bound ||Λ||^2; pigeonhole gives a pair satisfying the selection inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of well-definedness of Subalgorithm 1c
nodes.statement: Note that the starting point $\matr{X}_{0}\in\mathbf{EUT}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$ in \autoref{alg:jacob-GU-G_c}. We see that $\matr{X}_{k}\in\mathbf{EUT}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$ for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$. By \Cref{lem:ProjGradSubmatrix_2}, \Cref{lemma-ai-sum-0_c} and $\matr{\Lambda}=\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\in\mathfrak{eut}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$, we get that \begin{align*}{\small \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(\|\partial h^{(U)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2 + \|\partial h^{(D)}_k(\matr{I}_2) \|^2\right)} &{\small= \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{i_ki_k} - \Lambda_{j_kj_k}|^2\right)}\\ &{\small = \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + m\sum_{1\leq i_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_ki_k}|^2 \geq \|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2.} \end{align*} Therefore, there exist an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k = h^{(U)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$ such that $m(m-1)\|\partial h_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\geq\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Iterates stay upper triangular so Λ is in eut_m; summing squared partial derivatives over pairs bounds ||Λ||^2.

nodes.name: Proof of the diagonal descent inequality
nodes.statement: We now prove the inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c-5} by \Cref{lemm:elemen_express_c}(iii) in three different cases shown in \Cref{remar:rho_setting_four_case_c}. \begin{itemize} \item If $\gamma_{1}=\gamma_{2} = 0$, it is clear that the inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c-5} is satisfied for any $\iota_{D}>0$.\\ \item If $\varpi\in[0,\varsigma_{D})$, we get that \begin{align*} &h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0) - h^{(D)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) =\frac{3}{4}\gamma_{1}(1-4\varpi) =\frac{3(1-4\varpi)}{8(1-\varpi)}|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)|\\ &\geq \frac{3(1-4\varpi)\varepsilon}{8(1-\varpi)}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\| =\frac{3(1-4\varpi)\varepsilon}{4\sqrt{5}(1-\varpi)}\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\\ &\geq\frac{3(1-4\varpi)\varepsilon}{4\sqrt{5}(1-\varpi)}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\| \geq\frac{3(1-4\varsigma_{D})\varepsilon}{4\sqrt{5}}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*} \item If $\varpi\in(\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}},+\infty]$, we similarly get the above inequality. \item If $\varpi\in [\varsigma_{D},\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}}]$, it is easy to verify that \begin{equation} \sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}}\geq \frac{\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{2} \left(\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}+\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right). \end{equation} Then, we get that \begin{align*} &h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0) - h^{(D)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) = \left(\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}-\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right)^2 =\frac{1}{2}|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)|\frac{\left|\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}-\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right|}{\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}+\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}}\\ &\geq \frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\frac{\left|\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}-\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right|}{\sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}}} \ \ (\textrm{by equation \cref{eq:inequa_rho_r4_c}})\\ &\geq\frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\| \frac{\left|\sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{1}}-\sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{2}}\right|\left(\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}+\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right)^{1/2}} {\sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}}}\\ &\geq\frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\||x_k^{*}-1|\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{{x_k^{*}}^2}} \geq\frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*} \end{itemize} Now we set $\iota_{D} = \min(\frac{3(1-4\varsigma_{D})\varepsilon}{4\sqrt{5}},\frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4})$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis over the three rules for x_k^* using the explicit form of h^(D); ι_D is the minimum of the case constants.

nodes.name: Fourth-root inequality for gamma_1, gamma_2
nodes.statement: \sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}}\geq \frac{\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{2} \left(\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}+\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right).
nodes.label: eq:inequa_rho_r4_c

nodes.name: Proof of the triangular descent inequality
nodes.statement: We prove that the inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c-3} is satisfied in two cases. \begin{itemize} \item If $h_k = h^{(U)}_{k}$, by \Cref{lemm:elemen_express_c}(i), we see that \begin{align*} g(\matr{X}_{k-1})-g(\matr{X}_{k}) &=h^{(U)}_{k}(0,0)-h^{(U)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) = \frac{1}{\alpha_{1}}(\alpha_{2}^2+\alpha_{3}^2)\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\|\partial h^{(U)}_{k}(0,0)\|\|(x_k^{*},y_k^{*})\| \geq\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*} \item If $h_k = h^{(L)}_{k}$, by \Cref{lemm:elemen_express_c}(ii), we see that \begin{align*} g(\matr{X}_{k-1})-g(\matr{X}_{k}) &=h^{(L)}_{k}(0,0)-h^{(L)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) = \frac{1}{\beta_{1}}(\beta_{2}^2+\beta_{3}^2)\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\|\partial h^{(L)}_{k}(0,0)\|\|(x_k^{*},y_k^{*})\| \geq\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*} \end{itemize} Now we set $\iota_{LU}=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: For U and L cases, the optimal decrease equals half the gradient norm times the step, bounded via the selection inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of the step size lower bound for triangular and diagonal transformations
nodes.statement: If $h_k=h^{(U)}_{k}$, we have \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|^2=\frac{\alpha_2^2+\alpha_3^2}{\alpha_1^2}\geq \frac{\|\partial h^{(U)}_{k}(0,0)\|^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{\alpha}^2}\geq \frac{\varepsilon^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{\alpha}^2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|^2, \end{align*} where $\mathrm{M}_{\alpha}$ is a fixed positive constant always satisfying $|\alpha_1|\leq\mathrm{M}_{\alpha}$. The case $h_k=h^{(L)}_{k}$ is similar. Now we prove the $h_k=h^{(D)}_{k}$ case. If $\varpi\in[0,\varsigma_{D})$, we have that \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|^2=\frac{5}{4}\geq\frac{5}{4}\frac{1}{4(\gamma_1^2+\gamma_2^2)} \|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)\|^2\geq\frac{5}{4}\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{0}^2} \|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|^2. \end{align*} The case $\varpi\in(\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}},+\infty]$ is similar. If $\varpi\in [\varsigma_{D},\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}}]$, we have \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|^2\geq (1-x_k^{*})^2\geq \frac{\gamma_1^2(1-\varpi)^2}{\mathrm{M}_{0}^2\mathrm{M}_\varpi^2}=\frac{\|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)\|^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{0}^2\mathrm{M}_\varpi^2}\geq\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{0}^2\mathrm{M}_\varpi^2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|^2, \end{align*} where $\mathrm{M}_\varpi$ is a fixed positive constant always satisfying $(1+\sqrt{\varpi})(1+\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varpi})\leq\mathrm{M}_\varpi$. We only need to set $\kappa^2$ to be the minimum of all the above corresponding positive constants. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on the transformation and the ratio ϖ, bounding ||Ψ*−I|| below by the partial derivative norm.

nodes.name: Product rule
nodes.statement: By the product rule, we see that $\nabla\textit{p}(\matr{Y})=\nabla\tilde{p}(\matr{Y}\matr{X})\matr{X}^{{\sf H}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the product rule to express ∇p via ∇p̃.

nodes.name: Substitute and conclude
nodes.statement: Then, by equation \cref{eq:eucli_grad_h}, we have that \begin{align*} \matr{X}\matr{X}^{{\sf H}}\matr{Y}^{{\sf H}}\nabla\textit{p}(\matr{Y}) = \matr{Y}^{{\sf H}}\matr{Y}\matr{X}(\matr{Y}\matr{X})^{{\sf H}}\nabla\tilde{p}(\matr{Y}\matr{X})\matr{X}^{{\sf H}}= 2\matr{Y}^{{\sf H}}\matr{Y}\matr{X}\sum_{\ell=1}^{\matrelem{L}}\Upsilon(\matr{W}^{(\ell)})\matr{X}^{{\sf H}}. \end{align*} Note that $\matr{X}$ is invertible. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute the gradient identity and use invertibility of X.

nodes.name: Alignment from update rule
nodes.statement: By \Cref{remark:condition_inner}, we see that \begin{equation} |\langle\vect{v}_{i,j},[\cos\phi_*\ \sin\phi_*]^{\sf T}\rangle| \geq\varsigma_{Q}\|\vect{v}_{i,j}\| \end{equation} always holds.
nodes.statement_short: Update rule 3 ensures φ* is aligned with v_{i,j}.

nodes.name: Apply the θ lemma
nodes.statement: By \Cref{lemm:g-theta} and the above inequality \cref{eq:condition_phi_2}, we get that \begin{align*} q(\theta_{*},\phi_{*})-q(0,0)&=q(\theta_{*},\phi_{*})-q(0,\phi_{*})\geq 2\sqrt{2}\left|\sin(\frac{\theta_*}{2})\right||\Gamma_{12}\cos\phi_*+\Gamma_{13}\sin\phi_*|\\ &\geq 2\sqrt{2} \varsigma_{Q}\left|\sin(\frac{\theta_*}{2})\right|\|\vect{v}_{i,j}\|. \end{align*} The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the bound for a cos 4θ + b sin 4θ and the alignment.

nodes.name: Reduce to the Hermitian case
nodes.statement: We only prove the case $(\cdot)^{{\blacklozenge}}=(\cdot)^{{\sf H}}$, the other case being similar.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to the conjugate-transpose case.

nodes.name: Apply q bound and selection inequality
nodes.statement: By \Cref{lem:p_theta_phi} and equation \cref{eq:partial_h_k}, we get that \begin{align*} h^{(Q)}_k(0,0)-h^{(Q)}_k(\theta_*,\phi_*) &\geq 2\sqrt{2}\varsigma_{Q} \left|\sin(\frac{\theta_{*}}{2})\right|\|\vect{v}_{i,j}\| = \frac{\varsigma_{Q}}{4} 2\sqrt{2}\left|\sin(\frac{\theta_{*}}{2})\right|\|\partial h^{(Q)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|\\ &\geq \frac{\varsigma_{Q}\varepsilon}{4} \|\Gmat{i}{j}{\matr{\Psi}_{k}^{*}}-\matr{I}_m\|\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Combine the increase of q with the partial derivative and selection inequality.

nodes.name: Set the constant
nodes.statement: We can set $\iota_{Q}=(\varsigma_{Q}\varepsilon)/{4}$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Take ι_Q = ς_Q ε / 4.

nodes.name: Aligned case
nodes.statement: If $\vect{v}_{i,j}$ and $\vect{w}_{i,j}$ satisfy inequality \cref{eq:condition_phi_1}, then inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c-4-3} can be proved by a similar method as for \cite[Lemma 7.2]{ULC2019}.
nodes.statement_short: If the alignment condition holds, argue as in the unitary-group lemma.

nodes.name: Non-aligned case
nodes.statement: Otherwise, if we set $[\cos\phi_*\ \sin\phi_*]^{\sf T}=\vect{v}_{i,j}/{\|\vect{v}_{i,j}\|}$ and find $\theta_*$ based on $\phi_*$, then \begin{align*} |\sin(4\theta_{*})|&=\frac{\left|\Gamma_{12}\cos\phi_*+\Gamma_{13}\sin\phi_*\right|}{\sqrt{\left(\Gamma_{12}\cos\phi_*+\Gamma_{13}\sin\phi_*\right)^2+\frac{1}{4}\left(\Gamma_{11}-\Gamma_{22}\cos^2\phi_*-\Gamma_{33}\sin^2\phi_*-\Gamma_{23}\sin(2\phi_*)\right)^2}}\\ &\geq \frac{\sqrt{\Gamma_{12}^2+\Gamma_{13}^2}}{2\sqrt{5}\mathrm{M}_{\Gamma}} =\frac{\|\partial h^{(Q)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|}{8\sqrt{5}\mathrm{M}_{\Gamma}} \geq \frac{\varepsilon}{8\sqrt{5}\mathrm{M}_{\Gamma}}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|. \end{align*} Note that \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\| = 2\sqrt{2}\left|\sin(\frac{\theta_{*}}{2})\right| \geq \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}|\sin(4\theta_{*})|. \end{align*} We only need to set $\kappa_{Q}=\frac{\sqrt{2}\varepsilon}{32\sqrt{5}\mathrm{M}_{\Gamma}}$ in this case. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise bound |sin 4θ*| and hence ||Ψ*−I|| below.

nodes.name: Bound |sin 4θ*|
nodes.statement: Otherwise, if we set $[\cos\phi_*\ \sin\phi_*]^{\sf T}=\vect{v}_{i,j}/{\|\vect{v}_{i,j}\|}$ and find $\theta_*$ based on $\phi_*$, then \begin{align*} |\sin(4\theta_{*})|&=\frac{\left|\Gamma_{12}\cos\phi_*+\Gamma_{13}\sin\phi_*\right|}{\sqrt{\left(\Gamma_{12}\cos\phi_*+\Gamma_{13}\sin\phi_*\right)^2+\frac{1}{4}\left(\Gamma_{11}-\Gamma_{22}\cos^2\phi_*-\Gamma_{33}\sin^2\phi_*-\Gamma_{23}\sin(2\phi_*)\right)^2}}\\ &\geq \frac{\sqrt{\Gamma_{12}^2+\Gamma_{13}^2}}{2\sqrt{5}\mathrm{M}_{\Gamma}} =\frac{\|\partial h^{(Q)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|}{8\sqrt{5}\mathrm{M}_{\Gamma}} \geq \frac{\varepsilon}{8\sqrt{5}\mathrm{M}_{\Gamma}}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound |sin 4θ*| by the gradient norm over M_Γ.

nodes.name: Relate ||Ψ*−I|| to sin 4θ*
nodes.statement: Note that \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\| = 2\sqrt{2}\left|\sin(\frac{\theta_{*}}{2})\right| \geq \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}|\sin(4\theta_{*})|. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Set κ_Q
nodes.statement: We only need to set $\kappa_{Q}=\frac{\sqrt{2}\varepsilon}{32\sqrt{5}\mathrm{M}_{\Gamma}}$ in this case. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Choose κ_Q accordingly.

nodes.name: Start with BCD-GLU
nodes.statement: We first prove the case of BCD-GLU algorithm.
nodes.statement_short: Treat the BCD-GLU case first.

nodes.name: Sufficient descent of g
nodes.statement: By \Cref{lemma:global_rho_c,lemma:global_rho_c-2}, we see that \begin{equation} g(\matr{X}_{k-1})-g(\matr{X}_{k})\geq\min(\sigma_{D},\sigma_{LU})\|\ProjGrad{g}{\matr{X}_{k-1}}\|\|\matr{X}_{k}-\matr{X}_{k-1}\|, \end{equation} whenever the elementary function $h_k=h^{(D)}_{k}, h^{(U)}_{k}$ or $h^{(L)}_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the D and L/U corollaries into one descent inequality for g.

nodes.name: Sufficient descent of f
nodes.statement: By the above inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c-5-0-proof-7.1} and \Cref{lemma:line_search}, we have that \begin{equation} f(\matr{\omega}_{k-1})-f(\matr{\omega}_{k})\geq\min(\sigma_{D},\sigma_{LU},\sigma_{p})\|\ProjGrad{f_{t_k}}{\matr{\omega}_{k-1}}\|\|\matr{\omega}_{k}-\matr{\omega}_{k-1}\| \end{equation} always holds in BCD-GLU algorithm, which is the inequality \cref{eq:sufficient_descent-2} in \Cref{theorem-SU15-2}, if we set $\sigma=\min(\sigma_{D},\sigma_{LU},\sigma_{p})$.
nodes.statement_short: With the line search lemma, obtain the block sufficient descent condition.

nodes.name: Accumulation point is limit
nodes.statement: Therefore, if $\matr{\omega}_*$ is an accumulation point of the iterates $\{\matr{\omega}_k\}_{k\geq 1}$ produced by BCD-GLU algorithms, it is the limit point.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the BCD-G global convergence criterion.

nodes.name: Existence of accumulation point
nodes.statement: Note that the iterates $\{\matr{\omega}_k\}_{k\geq 1}$ remain bounded by condition \cref{eq:condi_bounded_X_gene}. There exists an accumulation point $\matr{\omega}_*$ such that the iterates $\{\matr{\omega}_k\}_{k\geq 1}$ converge to $\matr{\omega}_{*}$.
nodes.statement_short: Boundedness gives an accumulation point, hence convergence.

nodes.name: Other cases
nodes.statement: For other two cases of BCD-GQU and BCD-GU algorithms, by \Cref{lemma:line_search}, \Cref{lemma:global_rho_c}, \Cref{lemma:global_rho_c-2} and \Cref{lemma:h_k_condition_SU}, we can similarly prove that the inequality \cref{eq:sufficient_descent-2} is always satisfied, if we set $\sigma=\min(\sigma_{D},\sigma_{LU},\sigma_{Q},\sigma_{p})$ and $\min(\sigma_{D},\sigma_{LU},\sigma_{p})$, respectively. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: BCD-GQU and BCD-GU are handled similarly with the Givens corollary.

nodes.name: Start with BCD-GLU
nodes.statement: We first prove the case of BCD-GLU algorithm.
nodes.statement_short: Treat the BCD-GLU case first.

nodes.name: Squared-gradient descent of g
nodes.statement: By \Cref{lemma:weak_rho_inequality_c}, we see that \begin{equation} g(\matr{X}_{k-1})-g(\matr{X}_{k})\geq\min(\eta_{D},\eta_{LU})\|\ProjGrad{g}{\matr{X}_{k-1}}\|^2, \end{equation} whenever the elementary function $h_k=h^{(D)}_{k}, h^{(U)}_{k}$ or $h^{(L)}_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the L/U/D squared-gradient corollary.

nodes.name: Squared-gradient descent of f
nodes.statement: By the above inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c-5-0-proof-7.1-43} and \Cref{lemma:line_search-2}, we have that \begin{equation} f(\matr{\omega}_{k-1})-f(\matr{\omega}_{k})\geq\min(\eta_{D},\eta_{LU},\eta_{p})\|\ProjGrad{f_{t_k}}{\matr{\omega}_{k-1}}\|^2 \end{equation} always holds in BCD-GLU algorithm, which is the inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c} in \Cref{theorem-weak-general_c}, if we set $\eta=\min(\eta_{D},\eta_{LU},\eta_{p})$.
nodes.statement_short: With the line search lemma obtain the weak convergence condition.

nodes.name: Stationarity
nodes.statement: Therefore, if $\matr{\omega}_*$ is an accumulation point of the iterates $\{\matr{\omega}_k\}_{k\geq 1}$ produced by BCD-GLU algorithm, then $\matr{\omega}_*$ is a stationary point.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the weak convergence criterion.

nodes.name: Other cases
nodes.statement: For other two cases of BCD-GQU and BCD-GU algorithms, by \Cref{lemma:weak_rho_inequality_c} and \Cref{lemma:weak_rho_inequality_c-4}, we can similarly prove that the inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c} is always satisfied, if we set $\eta=\min(\eta_{D},\eta_{LU},\eta_{Q},\eta_{p})$ and $\min(\eta_{D},\eta_{LU},\eta_{p})$, respectively. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: BCD-GQU and BCD-GU are handled similarly.

nodes.name: Directional derivative of h^(Q)
nodes.statement: Define a projection operator $\mathcal{P}_{i,j}: \mathbb{C}^{m\times m} \to\mathbb{C}^{2\times 2}$ extracting a submatrix of $\matr{X} \in \mathbb{C}^{m\times m}$ as in \cite[Eq. (3.7)]{ULC2019}, and $\mathcal{P}_{i,j}^{{\sf T}}: \mathbb{C}^{2\times 2} \to\mathbb{C}^{m\times m}$ the conjugate operator. For the elementary function $\hij{i}{j}{\matr{X}}$ defined in \cref{eq:elemn_func_h}, if $\matr{\Delta} \in \mathfrak{su}_2(\mathbb{C}) = \Tang{\matr{I}_2}{\SUNN{2}(\mathbb{C})}$, we have that \begin{align*} &\langle\matr{\Delta},\ProjGrad{\hij{i}{j}{\matr{X}}}{\matr{I}_2}\rangle_{\matr{I}_2} = \left.\left( \frac{d}{dt} \hij{i}{j}{\matr{X}} (\exp(t\matr{\Delta}) )\right)\right|_{t=0} \ \ (\text{by \Cref{lem:gra_rela_elem}(i)}) \\ &= \left.\left( \frac{d}{dt} g (\matr{X} \Gmat{i}{j}{\exp(t\matr{\Delta} )} )\right)\right|_{t=0} = \left.\left( \frac{d}{dt} g (\text{Exp}_{\matr{X}} (\matr{X}\mathcal{P}_{i,j}^{{\sf T}}(\matr{\Delta} )t )) \right)\right|_{t=0} \\ &= \langle\matr{X} \mathcal{P}_{i,j}^{{\sf T}}(\matr{\Delta}),\ProjGrad{g}{\matr{X}}\rangle_{\matr{X}} \ \ (\text{by equation}\ \cref{eq:gradient_exp_map})= \langle\matr{\Delta},\mathcal{P}_{i,j} (\matr{\Lambda})\rangle_{\matr{I}_2}, \end{align*} where $\text{Exp}_{\matr{X}}$ is the map defined in \cref{eq:Exp_x_sl}.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce P_{i,j} and compute ⟨Δ, grad h^(Q)⟩ via the exponential relation.

nodes.name: Identify the gradient
nodes.statement: Note that $\matr{\Delta} \in \mathfrak{su}_2(\mathbb{C})$ and $\ProjGrad{\hij{i}{j}{\matr{X}}}{\matr{I}_2} \in \mathfrak{su}_2(\mathbb{C})$. The result can be obtained by direct calculations.
nodes.statement_short: Both Δ and the gradient lie in su_2; read off the result.

nodes.name: Other elementary functions
nodes.statement: For other three elementary functions $h^{(U)}_{(i,j),\matr{X}}$, $h^{(L)}_{(i,j),\matr{X}}$ and $h^{(D)}_{(i,j),\matr{X}}$, similar as the above case, we can obtain the results by \Cref{lem:gra_rela_elem}(ii), \Cref{lem:gra_rela_elem}(iii) and \Cref{lem:gra_rela_elem}(iv), respectively. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: The U, L, D cases follow similarly from Lemma A.1(ii)-(iv).

nodes.name: (i) GLU class
nodes.statement: (i) We first prove the existence of such an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_{k}$ in \autoref{alg:jacobi-LU-G_c}. By \Cref{lem:ProjGradSubmatrix_2}, \Cref{lemma-ai-sum-0_c} and $\matr{\Lambda}=\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\in\mathfrak{sl}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$, we have that \begin{align*} &\sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(\|\partial h^{(U)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2+\|\partial h^{(L)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2+\|\partial h^{(D)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\right) \\ &= \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{j_ki_k}|^2\right) + m\sum_{1\leq i_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_ki_k}|^2 \geq \|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2. \end{align*} Therefore, there exist an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k=h^{(U)}_k, h^{(L)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$ such that $\frac{3}{2}m(m-1)\|\partial h_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\geq\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Existence of a suitable pair for Subalgorithm 1a.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: (i) We first prove the existence of such an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_{k}$ in \autoref{alg:jacobi-LU-G_c}.
nodes.statement_short: State the goal for the GLU class.

nodes.name: Sum of squared derivatives
nodes.statement: By \Cref{lem:ProjGradSubmatrix_2}, \Cref{lemma-ai-sum-0_c} and $\matr{\Lambda}=\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\in\mathfrak{sl}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$, we have that \begin{align*} &\sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(\|\partial h^{(U)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2+\|\partial h^{(L)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2+\|\partial h^{(D)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\right) \\ &= \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{j_ki_k}|^2\right) + m\sum_{1\leq i_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_ki_k}|^2 \geq \|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Sum of squared partial derivatives dominates ||Λ||^2.

nodes.name: Pigeonhole
nodes.statement: Therefore, there exist an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k=h^{(U)}_k, h^{(L)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$ such that $\frac{3}{2}m(m-1)\|\partial h_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\geq\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Some pair attains at least the average.

nodes.name: (ii) GQU class
nodes.statement: (ii) We now prove the existence in \autoref{alg:jacobi-LQ-G_c}. Similar as above, we get that \begin{align*} &\sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(\|\partial h^{(Q)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2+\|\partial h^{(U)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2 + \|\partial h^{(D)}_k(\matr{I}_2) \|^2\right) \\ &= \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}^{*} - \Lambda_{j_ki_k}|^2+|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{i_ki_k} - \Lambda_{j_kj_k}|^2\right)\\ &\geq \frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{j_ki_k}|^2\right) + m\sum_{1\leq i_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_ki_k}|^2 \geq \frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2. \end{align*} Therefore, there exists an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k =h^{(Q)}_k, h^{(U)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$ such that $\frac{3}{3-\sqrt{5}}m(m-1)\|\partial h_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\geq\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2.$ The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Existence of a suitable pair for Subalgorithm 1b.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: (ii) We now prove the existence in \autoref{alg:jacobi-LQ-G_c}.
nodes.statement_short: State the goal for the GQU class.

nodes.name: Sum of squared derivatives
nodes.statement: Similar as above, we get that \begin{align*} &\sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(\|\partial h^{(Q)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2+\|\partial h^{(U)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2 + \|\partial h^{(D)}_k(\matr{I}_2) \|^2\right) \\ &= \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}^{*} - \Lambda_{j_ki_k}|^2+|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{i_ki_k} - \Lambda_{j_kj_k}|^2\right)\\ &\geq \frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{j_ki_k}|^2\right) + m\sum_{1\leq i_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_ki_k}|^2 \geq \frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma A.2(i) to bound the sum below by (3−√5)/2 ||Λ||^2.

nodes.name: Pigeonhole
nodes.statement: Therefore, there exists an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k =h^{(Q)}_k, h^{(U)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$ such that $\frac{3}{3-\sqrt{5}}m(m-1)\|\partial h_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\geq\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2.$ The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Some pair attains the required bound.

nodes.name: Iterates stay in EUT
nodes.statement: Note that the starting point $\matr{X}_{0}\in\mathbf{EUT}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$ in \autoref{alg:jacob-GU-G_c}. We see that $\matr{X}_{k}\in\mathbf{EUT}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$ for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: Upper triangular start keeps all iterates in EUT_m.

nodes.name: Sum of squared derivatives
nodes.statement: By \Cref{lem:ProjGradSubmatrix_2}, \Cref{lemma-ai-sum-0_c} and $\matr{\Lambda}=\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\in\mathfrak{eut}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$, we get that \begin{align*}{\small \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(\|\partial h^{(U)}_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2 + \|\partial h^{(D)}_k(\matr{I}_2) \|^2\right)} &{\small= \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} \left(|\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + |\Lambda_{i_ki_k} - \Lambda_{j_kj_k}|^2\right)}\\ &{\small = \sum_{1\leq i_k<j_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_kj_k}|^2 + m\sum_{1\leq i_k\leq m} |\Lambda_{i_ki_k}|^2 \geq \|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2.} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Sum of squared U and D partial derivatives dominates ||Λ||^2.

nodes.name: Pigeonhole
nodes.statement: Therefore, there exist an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k = h^{(U)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$ such that $m(m-1)\|\partial h_k(\matr{I}_2)\|^2\geq\|\matr{\Lambda}\|^2$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Some pair satisfies the selection inequality.

nodes.name: Case setup
nodes.statement: We now prove the inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c-5} by \Cref{lemm:elemen_express_c}(iii) in three different cases shown in \Cref{remar:rho_setting_four_case_c}.
nodes.statement_short: Prove the inequality in the cases of Update rule 2.

nodes.name: Degenerate case
nodes.statement: If $\gamma_{1}=\gamma_{2} = 0$, it is clear that the inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c-5} is satisfied for any $\iota_{D}>0$.\\
nodes.statement_short: If γ1=γ2=0 the inequality is trivial.

nodes.name: Small ratio case
nodes.statement: If $\varpi\in[0,\varsigma_{D})$, we get that \begin{align*} &h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0) - h^{(D)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) =\frac{3}{4}\gamma_{1}(1-4\varpi) =\frac{3(1-4\varpi)}{8(1-\varpi)}|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)|\\ &\geq \frac{3(1-4\varpi)\varepsilon}{8(1-\varpi)}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\| =\frac{3(1-4\varpi)\varepsilon}{4\sqrt{5}(1-\varpi)}\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\\ &\geq\frac{3(1-4\varpi)\varepsilon}{4\sqrt{5}(1-\varpi)}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\| \geq\frac{3(1-4\varsigma_{D})\varepsilon}{4\sqrt{5}}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For ϖ < ς_D bound the decrease using x* = 1/2.

nodes.name: Large ratio case
nodes.statement: If $\varpi\in(\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}},+\infty]$, we similarly get the above inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric to the small-ratio case.

nodes.name: Intermediate ratio case
nodes.statement: If $\varpi\in [\varsigma_{D},\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}}]$, it is easy to verify that \begin{equation} \sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}}\geq \frac{\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{2} \left(\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}+\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right). \end{equation} Then, we get that \begin{align*} &h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0) - h^{(D)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) = \left(\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}-\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right)^2 =\frac{1}{2}|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)|\frac{\left|\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}-\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right|}{\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}+\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}}\\ &\geq \frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\frac{\left|\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}-\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right|}{\sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}}} \ \ (\textrm{by equation \cref{eq:inequa_rho_r4_c}})\\ &\geq\frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\| \frac{\left|\sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{1}}-\sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{2}}\right|\left(\sqrt{\gamma_{1}}+\sqrt{\gamma_{2}}\right)^{1/2}} {\sqrt[\leftroot{-3}\uproot{5}4]{\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}}}\\ &\geq\frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\||x_k^{*}-1|\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{{x_k^{*}}^2}} \geq\frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use the fourth-root inequality to bound the decrease at the minimizer.

nodes.name: Set ι_D
nodes.statement: Now we set $\iota_{D} = \min(\frac{3(1-4\varsigma_{D})\varepsilon}{4\sqrt{5}},\frac{\varepsilon\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varsigma_{D}}}{4})$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Take ι_D as the minimum of the case constants.

nodes.name: Two cases
nodes.statement: We prove that the inequality \cref{equation-condition-weak_c-3} is satisfied in two cases. \begin{itemize} \item If $h_k = h^{(U)}_{k}$, by \Cref{lemm:elemen_express_c}(i), we see that \begin{align*} g(\matr{X}_{k-1})-g(\matr{X}_{k}) &=h^{(U)}_{k}(0,0)-h^{(U)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) = \frac{1}{\alpha_{1}}(\alpha_{2}^2+\alpha_{3}^2)\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\|\partial h^{(U)}_{k}(0,0)\|\|(x_k^{*},y_k^{*})\| \geq\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*} \item If $h_k = h^{(L)}_{k}$, by \Cref{lemm:elemen_express_c}(ii), we see that \begin{align*} g(\matr{X}_{k-1})-g(\matr{X}_{k}) &=h^{(L)}_{k}(0,0)-h^{(L)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) = \frac{1}{\beta_{1}}(\beta_{2}^2+\beta_{3}^2)\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\|\partial h^{(L)}_{k}(0,0)\|\|(x_k^{*},y_k^{*})\| \geq\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Prove the inequality in the U and L cases.

nodes.name: U case
nodes.statement: If $h_k = h^{(U)}_{k}$, by \Cref{lemm:elemen_express_c}(i), we see that \begin{align*} g(\matr{X}_{k-1})-g(\matr{X}_{k}) &=h^{(U)}_{k}(0,0)-h^{(U)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) = \frac{1}{\alpha_{1}}(\alpha_{2}^2+\alpha_{3}^2)\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\|\partial h^{(U)}_{k}(0,0)\|\|(x_k^{*},y_k^{*})\| \geq\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use the explicit quadratic form of h^(U).

nodes.name: L case
nodes.statement: If $h_k = h^{(L)}_{k}$, by \Cref{lemm:elemen_express_c}(ii), we see that \begin{align*} g(\matr{X}_{k-1})-g(\matr{X}_{k}) &=h^{(L)}_{k}(0,0)-h^{(L)}_{k}(x_k^*,y_k^*) = \frac{1}{\beta_{1}}(\beta_{2}^2+\beta_{3}^2)\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\|\partial h^{(L)}_{k}(0,0)\|\|(x_k^{*},y_k^{*})\| \geq\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|\|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use the explicit quadratic form of h^(L).

nodes.name: Set ι_LU
nodes.statement: Now we set $\iota_{LU}=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Take ι_LU = ε/2.

nodes.name: Triangular cases
nodes.statement: If $h_k=h^{(U)}_{k}$, we have \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|^2=\frac{\alpha_2^2+\alpha_3^2}{\alpha_1^2}\geq \frac{\|\partial h^{(U)}_{k}(0,0)\|^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{\alpha}^2}\geq \frac{\varepsilon^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{\alpha}^2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|^2, \end{align*} where $\mathrm{M}_{\alpha}$ is a fixed positive constant always satisfying $|\alpha_1|\leq\mathrm{M}_{\alpha}$. The case $h_k=h^{(L)}_{k}$ is similar.
nodes.statement_short: For h^(U) (and similarly h^(L)) bound ||Ψ*−I|| via α's.

nodes.name: Diagonal case
nodes.statement: Now we prove the $h_k=h^{(D)}_{k}$ case. If $\varpi\in[0,\varsigma_{D})$, we have that \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|^2=\frac{5}{4}\geq\frac{5}{4}\frac{1}{4(\gamma_1^2+\gamma_2^2)} \|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)\|^2\geq\frac{5}{4}\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{0}^2} \|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|^2. \end{align*} The case $\varpi\in(\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}},+\infty]$ is similar. If $\varpi\in [\varsigma_{D},\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}}]$, we have \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|^2\geq (1-x_k^{*})^2\geq \frac{\gamma_1^2(1-\varpi)^2}{\mathrm{M}_{0}^2\mathrm{M}_\varpi^2}=\frac{\|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)\|^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{0}^2\mathrm{M}_\varpi^2}\geq\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{0}^2\mathrm{M}_\varpi^2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|^2, \end{align*} where $\mathrm{M}_\varpi$ is a fixed positive constant always satisfying $(1+\sqrt{\varpi})(1+\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varpi})\leq\mathrm{M}_\varpi$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound ||Ψ*−I|| for each regime of ϖ.

nodes.name: Extreme ratio
nodes.statement: If $\varpi\in[0,\varsigma_{D})$, we have that \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|^2=\frac{5}{4}\geq\frac{5}{4}\frac{1}{4(\gamma_1^2+\gamma_2^2)} \|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)\|^2\geq\frac{5}{4}\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{0}^2} \|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|^2. \end{align*} The case $\varpi\in(\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}},+\infty]$ is similar.
nodes.statement_short: For extreme ϖ, ||Ψ*−I||^2 = 5/4.

nodes.name: Intermediate ratio
nodes.statement: If $\varpi\in [\varsigma_{D},\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}}]$, we have \begin{align*} \|\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}-\matr{I}_{2}\|^2\geq (1-x_k^{*})^2\geq \frac{\gamma_1^2(1-\varpi)^2}{\mathrm{M}_{0}^2\mathrm{M}_\varpi^2}=\frac{\|\partial h^{(D)}_{k}(1,0)\|^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{0}^2\mathrm{M}_\varpi^2}\geq\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4\mathrm{M}_{0}^2\mathrm{M}_\varpi^2}\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|^2, \end{align*} where $\mathrm{M}_\varpi$ is a fixed positive constant always satisfying $(1+\sqrt{\varpi})(1+\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varpi})\leq\mathrm{M}_\varpi$.
nodes.statement_short: For intermediate ϖ, bound (1−x*)^2 below.

nodes.name: Set κ
nodes.statement: We only need to set $\kappa^2$ to be the minimum of all the above corresponding positive constants. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Take κ^2 as the minimum constant.

nodes.name: Iterate over k
nodes.statement: \FOR{$k=1,2,\cdots,$} \STATE Choose $t_k=1$ or $2$ such that the Riemannian gradients satisfy \begin{equation} \|\ProjGrad{f_{t_k}}{\matr{\omega}_{k-1}}\|\geq\upsilon\|\ProjGrad{f}{\matr{\omega}_{k-1}}\|; \end{equation} \vspace{-0.5cm} \IF {$t_k=1$} \STATE Update $\matr{Y}_{k}$ using the line search descent method (cf. \Cref{subsec:line_seach}); \STATE Set $\matr{X}_{k}=\matr{X}_{k-1}$; \ELSE \STATE Set $\matr{Y}_{k}=\matr{Y}_{k-1}$; \STATE Update $\matr{X}_{k}$ using elementary transformations (cf. \autoref{alg:jacobi-LU-G_c} to \ref{alg:jacob-GU-G_c}). \ENDIF

nodes.name: Choose block t_k
nodes.statement: Choose $t_k=1$ or $2$ such that the Riemannian gradients satisfy \begin{equation} \|\ProjGrad{f_{t_k}}{\matr{\omega}_{k-1}}\|\geq\upsilon\|\ProjGrad{f}{\matr{\omega}_{k-1}}\|; \end{equation} \vspace{-0.5cm}
nodes.statement_short: Pick the block whose Riemannian gradient is at least υ times the full gradient.
nodes.label: eq:inequality_BCD_G

nodes.name: If block 1
nodes.statement: \IF {$t_k=1$} \STATE Update $\matr{Y}_{k}$ using the line search descent method (cf. \Cref{subsec:line_seach}); \STATE Set $\matr{X}_{k}=\matr{X}_{k-1}$;

nodes.name: Line search update of Y
nodes.statement: Update $\matr{Y}_{k}$ using the line search descent method (cf. \Cref{subsec:line_seach});
nodes.statement_short: Update Y_k by the line search descent method on the Stiefel manifold.

nodes.name: Keep X
nodes.statement: Set $\matr{X}_{k}=\matr{X}_{k-1}$;

nodes.name: Else block 2
nodes.statement: \ELSE \STATE Set $\matr{Y}_{k}=\matr{Y}_{k-1}$; \STATE Update $\matr{X}_{k}$ using elementary transformations (cf. \autoref{alg:jacobi-LU-G_c} to \ref{alg:jacob-GU-G_c}).

nodes.name: Keep Y
nodes.statement: Set $\matr{Y}_{k}=\matr{Y}_{k-1}$;

nodes.name: Elementary transformation update of X
nodes.statement: Update $\matr{X}_{k}$ using elementary transformations (cf. \autoref{alg:jacobi-LU-G_c} to \ref{alg:jacob-GU-G_c}).
nodes.statement_short: Update X_k by one of Subalgorithms 1a-1c.

nodes.name: Iterate over k
nodes.statement: \FOR{$k=1,2,\cdots,$} \STATE Update $\matr{X}_k$ using elementary transformations (cf. \autoref{alg:jacobi-LU-G_c} to \ref{alg:jacobi-LQ-G_c}).

nodes.name: Elementary transformation update
nodes.statement: Update $\matr{X}_k$ using elementary transformations (cf. \autoref{alg:jacobi-LU-G_c} to \ref{alg:jacobi-LQ-G_c}).
nodes.statement_short: Update X_k by Subalgorithm 1a or 1b.

nodes.name: Choose pair and elementary function
nodes.statement: \quad Choose an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k$ such that\footnote{The inequality \cref{eq-inequality-G-LU_c} can be seen as a non-orthogonal analogue of \cite[Eq. (3.3)]{IshtAV13:simax} and \cite[Eq. (10)]{LUC2017globally}.} \begin{equation} \|\partial h_k(\matr{I}_2)\| \geq\varepsilon\|\matr{\Lambda}(\matr{X}_{k-1})\|, \end{equation} \quad where $h_k=h^{(U)}_k, h^{(L)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$;
nodes.statement_short: Select (i_k,j_k) and h_k whose derivative at I_2 is at least ε||Λ(X_{k-1})||.
nodes.label: eq-inequality-G-LU_c

nodes.name: Minimize elementary function
nodes.statement: \quad Compute $\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}$ that minimizes the elementary function $h_k$, satisfying \Cref{remar:rho_setting_four_case_ul} and \ref{remar:rho_setting_four_case_c} (will be shown in \Cref{sec:trian_diago_rotation});
nodes.statement_short: Compute the minimizer Ψ*_k of h_k following the update rules.

nodes.name: Multiplicative update
nodes.statement: \quad Update $\matr{X}_k = \matr{X}_{k-1}\matr{P}_{k}$, where $\matr{P}_{k}=\Umat{i_k}{j_k}{\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}}, \Lmat{i_k}{j_k}{\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}}$ or $\Dmat{i_k}{j_k}{\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}}$.
nodes.statement_short: X_k = X_{k-1} P_k with the chosen elementary transformation.

nodes.name: Choose pair and elementary function
nodes.statement: \quad Choose an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k$ satisfying the inequality \cref{eq-inequality-G-LU_c}, where $h_k =h^{(Q)}_k, h^{(U)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$;
nodes.statement_short: Select (i_k,j_k) and h_k whose derivative at I_2 is at least ε||Λ(X_{k-1})||.

nodes.name: Minimize elementary function
nodes.statement: \quad Compute $\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}$ that minimizes the elementary function $h_k$, satisfying \Cref{remar:rho_setting_four_case_ul}, \ref{remar:rho_setting_four_case_c} and \ref{remark:condition_inner} (will be shown in \Cref{sec:trian_diago_rotation,sec:trian_diago_rotation-2});
nodes.statement_short: Compute the minimizer Ψ*_k of h_k following the update rules.

nodes.name: Multiplicative update
nodes.statement: \quad Update $\matr{X}_k = \matr{X}_{k-1}\matr{P}_{k}$, where $\matr{P}_{k}=\Gmat{i_k}{j_k}{\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}}, \Umat{i_k}{j_k}{\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}}$ or $\Dmat{i_k}{j_k}{\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}}$.
nodes.statement_short: X_k = X_{k-1} P_k with the chosen elementary transformation.

nodes.name: Choose pair and elementary function
nodes.statement: \quad Choose an index pair $(i_k,j_k)$ and an elementary function $h_k$ satisfying the inequality \cref{eq-inequality-G-LU_c}, where $h_k=h^{(U)}_k$ or $h^{(D)}_k$;
nodes.statement_short: Select (i_k,j_k) and h_k whose derivative at I_2 is at least ε||Λ(X_{k-1})||.

nodes.name: Minimize elementary function
nodes.statement: \quad Compute $\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}$ that minimizes the elementary function $h_k$, satisfying \Cref{remar:rho_setting_four_case_ul} and \ref{remar:rho_setting_four_case_c} (will be shown in \Cref{sec:trian_diago_rotation});
nodes.statement_short: Compute the minimizer Ψ*_k of h_k following the update rules.

nodes.name: Multiplicative update
nodes.statement: \quad Update $\matr{X}_k = \matr{X}_{k-1}\matr{P}_{k}$, where $\matr{P}_{k}=\Umat{i_k}{j_k}{\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}}$ or $\Dmat{i_k}{j_k}{\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}}$.
nodes.statement_short: X_k = X_{k-1} P_k with the chosen elementary transformation.

nodes.name: U case rule
nodes.statement: we see that $x_{k}^{*}=0$ if $\alpha_{1}\neq0$ and $\alpha_{2}=0$. It is not possible that $\alpha_{1}=0$ and $\alpha_{2}\neq0$. If $\alpha_{1}=\alpha_{2}=0$, we set $x_{k}^{*}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: For h^(U), x* = 0 when α2 = 0 (and by convention when α1 = α2 = 0).

nodes.name: L case rule
nodes.statement: In the case of $h_k=h^{(L)}_{k}$, we make the similar update rules for the value of $y_{k}^{*}$.
nodes.statement_short: Analogous rule for h^(L).

nodes.name: Set y*=0
nodes.statement: if $h_k=h^{(D)}_{k}$, we always set $y_k^{*}=0$.

nodes.name: Degenerate case
nodes.statement: If $\gamma_{1}=\gamma_{2} = 0$, we set $x_k^{*}=0$.

nodes.name: Extreme ratio
nodes.statement: Let $\varpi\stackrel{\sf def}{=}\frac{\gamma_{2}}{\gamma_{1}}$. If $\varpi\in[0,\varsigma_{D})$, we set $x_k^{*}=\frac{1}{2}$. If $\varpi\in(\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}},+\infty]$, we set $x_k^{*}=2$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute ϖ=γ2/γ1; take x*=1/2 or 2 for extreme ratios.

nodes.name: Intermediate ratio
nodes.statement: Otherwise, if $\varpi\in[\varsigma_{D},\frac{1}{\varsigma_{D}}]$, we set $x_k^{*}=\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{4}4]{\varpi}$, which is the minimum point.
nodes.statement_short: Take x* = ϖ^{1/4}, the minimizer.

nodes.name: Top eigenvector
nodes.statement: we find the eigenvector $\vect{u}$ of $\matr{\Gamma}$ corresponding to the largest eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Alignment vectors
nodes.statement: Define two vectors $\vect{v}_{i,j}\stackrel{\sf def}{=}\left[\Gamma_{12},\ \Gamma_{13}\right]^{\sf T}\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\vect{w}_{i,j}\stackrel{\sf def}{=} \left[u_2,\ u_3\right]^{\sf T}\in\mathbb{R}^2.$
nodes.statement_short: Form v_{i,j} from Γ and w_{i,j} from u.

nodes.name: Aligned branch
nodes.statement: If it holds that \begin{equation} |\langle\vect{v}_{i,j},\vect{w}_{i,j}\rangle| \geq\varsigma_{Q}\|\vect{v}_{i,j}\|\|\vect{w}_{i,j}\|, \end{equation} then we find $\phi_*$ and $\theta_*$ by setting $\vect{r}=\vect{u}$, and $\matr{\Psi}^{*}_{k}=\matr{\Psi}(\theta_*,\phi_*)$;
nodes.statement_short: If aligned, set r = u to obtain (θ*,φ*).

nodes.name: Non-aligned branch
nodes.statement: Otherwise, we set $[\cos\phi_*,\ \sin\phi_*]^{\sf T}=\vect{v}_{i,j}/{\|\vect{v}_{i,j}\|}$, and then calculate $\theta_*$, which maximizes the restricted function $q(\theta,\phi_{*})$.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise fix φ* along v_{i,j} and maximize q over θ.
